## Spatial & Geometric Definition
* Geometry Type: Polygon (Wetland_Restoration_Polygon).

* Spatial Delineation: Shallow-water aquatic marsh and bottomland wetland zones restored through grading, embankment construction, or river stage management.

* Wetland Classes: Emergent hemi-marsh, deep-water marsh, scrub-shrub wetland, and wet meadow.

### Primary Restoration & Engineering Objectives
* Hemi-Marsh Restoration: Create balanced 50:50 ratios of dense emergent vegetation to open-water pools, maximizing wildlife diversity and nesting cover.

* Nutrient & Silt Cycling: Serve as natural bio-retention filters that sequester suspended sediment, nitrogen, and phosphorus from passing floodwaters.

* Amphibian & Reptile Nursery: Provide predator-sheltered, warm, sunlit nursery waters for amphibians, shorebirds, and native aquatic reptiles.

### Typical Cross-Sections, Dimensions & Sizing Criteria
* Water Depth Zonation:Littoral Shelf (0.0 to 1.0 ft depth): Supports emergent marsh species (Typha latifolia, Sagittaria latifolia, Scirpus spp.).

* Intermediate Zone (1.0 to 3.0 ft depth): Promotes diverse beds of submersed aquatic vegetation (SAV) (Vallisneria americana, Potamogeton spp.).

* Deep Pools (4.0 to 6.0 ft depth): Overwintering survival pockets for turtles and amphibians.

* Micro-Topographic Diversity: Irregular curving shorelines, isolated mud islands, and variable bottom elevations to eliminate uniform bathymetry.

### Construction & Implementation Methodology
* Low-Ground-Pressure Earthmoving: Wide-track bulldozers (<3 psi ground pressure) shaping undulating bottoms and shallow perimeter benches.

* Vegetation Transplants & Hydroseeding: Installation of pre-rooted emergent wetland plugs and broadcast wetland seed mixes immediately following final earthwork.

### Quality Control, Inspection & Long-Term Maintenance
* Hydro-Period Monitoring: Continuous pressure transducer stage recorders logging water depths throughout the year to confirm hydrologic permanence.

* Invasive Species Eradication: Rigorous annual mechanical mowing and aquatic herbicide treatments targeting narrowleaf cattail and purple loosestrife.


## Spatial Feature Attribute
### Definition
Geospatial feature composed of one unique wetland class (no complexes), used to determine USACE jurisdiction and regulatory impacts. Each feature represents a single, homogeneous wetland type suitable for regulatory and design analysis.

### Purpose
Wetland features document the location, extent, and type of wetlands affected by or created through restoration projects. They support regulatory determinations, impact assessments, mitigation planning, and design of floodplain restoration measures intended to improve natural floodplain function and habitat.

### Applicability
Wetland features are applicable wherever wetlands occur within Upper Mississippi River System (UMRS) restoration project areas or where wetlands are created, restored, or enhanced as part of project actions. They are used to assess regulatory jurisdiction, quantify impacts and benefits, and guide design and management of floodplain restoration measures. (UMRR Design Handbook, 2012)

### Notes
Restoration features now have a Program_UID field to distinguish between NESP and UMRR features. Aliases without program identification will be created for any field that currently has UMRR in the name, so they can be used for NESP or UMRR data.

Attribute criteria for each field includes the following:

* Attribute Status – defines whether the field requires a value or if it is optional based on available information.
* Phases – indicates the earliest time in the project lifecycle values for this attribute are available.
* Digitizing requirements – indicates when the field value should be entered in the attribute table.

Geometry Note: No Z values are needed for this feature.

### Wetland
(polygon) – Geospatial feature composed of one unique wetland class (no complexes) used to determine USACE jurisdiction and regulatory impacts.

## Parameters

### Program_UID
Designate program NESP or UMRR.

### Project_ID (alias: PROJECT_ID)
Foreign key to the unique NESP/UMRR project ID.

### Type (alias)
A broad classification used to group NESP/UMRR restoration features into categories of similar function.

<table class="table-grid">
  <thead>
    <tr>
      <th>Value</th>
      <th>Description</th>
    </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr>
      <td>Floodplain Restoration</td>
      <td>Measures taken to improve natural floodplain function and habitat.</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>Island Creation</td>
      <td>Measures taken to create or restore islands in rivers.</td>
    </tr>
  </tbody>
</table>

### SubType (alias: Subtype)
A classification used to group NESP/UMRR restoration features into specific wetland design feature categories.

<table class="table-grid">
  <thead>
    <tr>
      <th>Value</th>
      <th>Description</th>
    </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr>
      <td>Depressional wetland</td>
      <td>Wetland occurring in a topographic depression, typically ponded or seasonally flooded, with limited surface outlet and water supplied by precipitation, runoff, and/or groundwater.</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>Mudflat</td>
      <td>Shallow, frequently exposed wetland surface characterized by fine sediments and periodic inundation, often used by shorebirds and other wildlife.</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>Swale</td>
      <td>Shallow, elongated wetland feature that conveys or temporarily stores water, often oriented along low-lying topographic features within the floodplain.</td>
    </tr>
  </tbody>
</table>

### RestorFeatStatus
A description of the status of the individual restoration. It also includes the party responsible for the individual feature.

<table class="table-grid">
  <thead>
    <tr>
      <th>Value</th>
      <th>Description</th>
    </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr>
      <td>USACE Planned</td>
      <td>Feature is in a USACE planning stage.</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>USACE Built</td>
      <td>Feature has been built by USACE. If a feature has been planned and built by USACE, once constructed, it will always be considered USACE built even if it has been repaired under later project stages.</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>USACE Enhanced</td>
      <td>The function of an existing feature that was not built by USACE has been enhanced by a feature that was USACE built or repaired.</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>USACE Repaired</td>
      <td>An existing feature that was not built by USACE has been directly improved or repaired.</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>Other Planned</td>
      <td>A feature that is planned by another organization or government agency.</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>Other Built</td>
      <td>Feature has been built by another organization or government agency and is an integral part of the UMRR project.</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>Other Enhanced</td>
      <td>The function of an existing feature, that was built by another organization or government agency, has been enhanced by a feature that was built or repaired by a non-USACE organization or government agency.</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>Other Repaired</td>
      <td>An existing feature that has been directly improved or repaired by another organization or government agency.</td>
    </tr>
  </tbody>
</table>

### sdsFeatureName
The common name of the feature.

### sdsFeatureDescription
A narrative describing the feature.

### RestorFeatVdatum
Vertical datum of elevations recorded in the attribute table or used as feature z values.

<table class="table-grid">
  <thead>
    <tr>
      <th>Value</th>
      <th>Description</th>
    </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr>
      <td>MSL 1912</td>
      <td>Mean Sea Level of 1912</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>NGVD 1929</td>
      <td>National Geodetic Vertical Datum of 1929</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>NAVD 1988</td>
      <td>North American Vertical Datum of 1988</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>Other</td>
      <td>Other, note datum in sdsFeatureDescription</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>Unknown</td>
      <td>Unknown vertical datum</td>
    </tr>
  </tbody>
</table>

### HydroGeoMorphType
The hydrogeomorphology of the wetland.

<table class="table-grid">
  <thead>
    <tr>
      <th>Value</th>
      <th>Description</th>
    </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr>
      <td>Depressional</td>
      <td>Characterized by a water source consisting of return flow from groundwater and interflow with primarily vertical hydrodynamics.</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>Estuarine Fringe</td>
      <td>Water source consists of overbank flow from estuaries, with bidirectional and horizontal hydrodynamics being dominant.</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>Lacustrine Fringe</td>
      <td>Dominant water source is lake overbank flow, and the dominant hydrodynamics are bidirectional and horizontal.</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>Mineral Soil Flats</td>
      <td>Water source is precipitation, and vertical hydrodynamics are dominant.</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>Organic Soil Flats</td>
      <td>Water source is precipitation, and the dominant hydrodynamics are vertical.</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>Riverine</td>
      <td>Characterized by a water source of overbank flow from a channel, with predominantly unidirectional and horizontal hydrodynamics.</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>Slope</td>
      <td>Characterized by a water source of return flow from groundwater, with principally unidirectional and horizontal hydrodynamics.</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>Other</td>
      <td>Other hydrogeomorphic setting; specify in sdsFeatureDescription.</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>NA</td>
      <td>Not applicable.</td>
    </tr>
  </tbody>
</table>

### DepthMaxFT
Maximum depth in feet of the constructed wetland.

### DepthAverageFT
Average depth in feet of the constructed wetland.

### Acres
Area of the wetland in acres.

### sdsMetaDataID
References attached metadata.

### RestorFeatIDPK
Primary key used to uniquely identify the restoration feature record.

### sdsID
Identifier used to link the feature to supporting SDS (spatial data system) records or related datasets.

### mediaIDFK
Foreign key used to reference associated media (e.g., photographs, design drawings, as-built plans) documenting the wetland.
